DECISION 

I. 
INTRODUCTION 
A. 
SUMMARY 
The Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (Authority or PURA) establishes the 
Customer Legal Advocacy Services Program (CLAS Program or Program), including an 
application and approval process to distribute up to $1 million annually to organizations 
or individuals providing services with the express purpose of attaining participation in 
public service company (PSC) programs that assist customers with utility bill or arrearage 
payments as contemplated in General Statutes § 16-262(b)(8), as amended by Public Act 
23-102, § 30. 

The Program will enable organizations or individuals interested in providing such 
services to apply to be included on the Program’s qualified provider list (QPL). Providers 
who meet the requirements of the program and are approved to participate as indicated 
by the QPL (Providers) would then be able to seek reimbursement according to the 
program parameters outlined herein starting on January 1, 2025. 

This docket will also serve as the administrative record for applications for the QPL, 
as well as for reimbursement submissions from eligible providers. 
B. 
BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING 
The Authority may distribute up to $1 million annually to organizations or 
individuals providing services to utility customers with the express purpose of enrolling 
customers in PSC programs that provide utility bill assistance or arrearage payments, 
including negotiating a reasonable amortization payment plan. General Statutes § 16-
262c(b). 
The Authority sought initial input from participants on various topics relating to the 
legal services provisions included in Public Act 23-102 § 30. Notice of Request for Written 
Comments, Sept. 7, 2023, Docket No. 23-05-01, Annual Review of Affordability Programs 
and Offerings (Energy Affordability Annual Review).1 On September 25, 2023, The 
Connecticut Light and Power Company d/b/a Eversource Energy (Eversource), Yankee 
Gas Services Company (YGS),2 The Office of Consumer Counsel (OCC), PURA’s Office 
of Education, Outreach, and Enforcement (EOE), and the Center for Children’s Advocacy 
(CCA) provided comments for consideration. 

1 Stakeholder comments from Docket No. 23-05-01 were admitted into the evidentiary record of this 
proceeding on March 15, 2024. 
2 Eversource and YGS filed joint written comments. 

Docket No. 23-11-04 

Page 2 

C. 
CONDUCT OF THE PROCEEDING 
On February 6, 2024, the Authority initiated this docket to establish a program to 
distribute such funds to organizations or individuals providing legal services to utility 
customers. 
On April 5, 2024, the Authority issued a Notice of Issuance of Straw Proposal and 
Request for Written Comments in the instant proceeding, accompanied by three 
appendices outlining draft Program implementation documents. See Notice of Issuance 
of Straw Proposal and Request for Written Comments; Appendix A; Appendix B; 
Appendix C; Appendix D. 
Eversource, YGS, The United Illuminating Company (UI), the Southern 
Connecticut Gas Company (SCG), Connecticut Natural Gas Corporation (CNG), and 
Aquarion Water Company of Connecticut (Aquarion) filed joint comments on the Straw 
Proposal. See Eversource, YGS, UI, SCG, CNG, and Aquarion Comments, Apr. 19, 2024 
(Joint Public Service Companies, or PSC Comments). OCC and CCA also submitted 
Written Comments. See OCC Comments, Apr. 19, 2024 (OCC Comments); and CCA 
Comments, Apr. 19, 2024 (CCA Comments). 
The Authority issued a proposed final decision in this matter on May 29, 2024. All 
participants were given the opportunity to file written exceptions to the proposed final 
decision. 

D. 
PARTICIPANTS 
The Authority recognized the following as Participants in the proceeding: UI, SCG, 
and CNG, 180 Marsh Hill Road, Orange, CT 06477; Eversource, YGS, and Aquarion, 
P.O. Box 270, Hartford, CT 06410; OCC, Ten Franklin Square, New Britain, CT 06051; 
the Commissioner of the Department of Energy and Environmental Protection; EOE, Ten 
Franklin Square, New Britain, CT 06105; Connecticut Water Company, 93 West Main 
Street, Clinton, CT 06413; and CCA, 65 Elizabeth Street, Hartford, CT 06105. 
E. 
ALIGNMENT WITH REGULATORY OBJECTIVES 
The Authority created a framework for investigating methods for realizing an 
equitable modern electric grid in Connecticut (EMG Framework), as well as for near-term 
and long-term plans to ensure continued developments to Connecticut’s electric grid. 
Decision, Oct. 2, 2019, Docket No. 17-12-03, PURA Investigation into Distribution System 
Planning of the Electric Distribution Companies (EMG Decision). 

PURA established the following objectives for its EMG Framework: 

1. Support (or remove barriers to) the growth of Connecticut’s green economy; 
2. Enable a cost-effective, economy-wide transition to a decarbonized future; 
3. Enhance customer access to a more resilient, reliable, and secure commodity; and 
4. Advance the ongoing energy affordability dialogue in the state, particularly in 
underserved communities. 

Docket No. 23-11-04 

Page 3 

EMG Decision, p. 26. 

Additionally, the Authority established four overarching regulatory objectives to 
guide the development of a comprehensive performance-based regulation (PBR) 
framework:3 

1. Excellent Operational Performance: Achieve the highest standards for EDC 
performance in terms of efficiency, reliability, resiliency, and supply; 
2. Public Policy Achievement: Meet state-level GHG emissions, decarbonization, and 
DER deployment targets, and enhance environmental protection and equity 
measures; 
3. Customer Empowerment and Satisfaction: Beyond traditional customer 
satisfaction metrics, empower EDC customers to take greater control of their 
energy services (e.g., deploying DERs and other grid-edge technologies, reducing 
their carbon footprint, etc.) and expenditures (e.g., lowering their monthly utility 
bill); and 
4. Reasonable, Equitable, and Affordable Rates: Ensure customers across all 
socioeconomic classes receive reasonable rates and equitable access to the same 
products and services. 

Decision, Apr. 26, 2023, Docket No. 21-05-15, PURA Investigation into a Performance 
Based Regulation Framework for the Electric Distribution Companies (PBR Phase 1 
Decision), p. 13. 

The objectives outlined in the PBR Framework are rooted in and have broad 
applicability to all utility regulatory matters and, as such, are designed to guide current 
and future utility regulation in Connecticut. Id., p. 11. Further, the Authority developed 
these regulatory goals to be inclusive of the four objectives of the EMG Framework and 
legacy regulatory goals of safe, reliable, and affordable service. Id., p. 13. 

The CLAS Program directly supports EMG Framework Objective 4, as well as the 
third and fourth regulatory goals established through the PBR Phase 1 Decision. 
Specifically, the CLAS Program will provide an additional tool for underserved customers 
to access and navigate the available programs offered by PSCs and to negotiate 
reasonable amortization payment plans; thereby furthering energy affordability and 
enhancing customers’ ability to control their energy expenditures. 

3 The PBR Phase 1 Decision was issued pursuant to Public Act 20-5, §1 (Take Back Our Grid Act). 

Docket No. 23-11-04 

Page 4 

F. 
STAKEHOLDER COMMENTS 
The Authority sought initial feedback on whether an annual or rolling application 
process would be appropriate. Eversource recommended a rolling process. Eversource 
Comments, Sept. 25, 2023, Docket No. 23-05-01, p. 4. EOE suggested an annual 
application where Providers submit annual accounting compliance, as well as quarterly 
updates about the customers assisted under the program. EOE Comments, Sept. 25, 
2023, Docket No. 23-05-01, pp. 6-7. CCA proposed a quarterly application process that 
would allow flexibility due to Authority or legislative actions that necessitate additional 
customer support. CCA Comments, Sept. 25, 2023, Docket No. 23-05-01, p. 4. 

Eversource proposed that funding be disbursed as reimbursements to Providers, 
which would allow the Authority to evaluate invoices, ensure that fees are appropriate, 
and ask questions. Eversource, Sept. 25, 2023, Docket No. 23-05-01, Comments, p. 4. 
Further, Eversource noted that it is standard practice for attorneys to submit invoices for 
payment after services have been provided. Id. EOE agreed that funds should be 
disbursed after a customer received services, noting such a practice would also inform 
the Authority about which utility’s customers were served. EOE, Sept. 25, 2023, Docket 
No. 23-05-01, Comments, p. 8. CCA opined that funds should be disbursed in advance 
of providing services, as they would not otherwise have funding available to provide 
services. CCA, Sept. 25, 2023, Docket No. 23-05-01, Comments, p. 4. 

Based on this stakeholder feedback, the Authority developed and issued a Straw 
Proposal and Request for Written Comments to further refine the Program. 

II. 
CLAS PROGRAM ELEMENTS 
The Authority has established or otherwise sought to improve the utilities’ 
affordability and arrearage forgiveness programs. See, e.g., Decision, Oct. 11, 2023, 
Docket No. 23-05-01, Annual Review of Affordability Program and Offerings (Energy 
Affordability Annual Review). The objective of the CLAS Program is to provide an 
augmentative resource for customers that will help to ensure that customers are able to 
access and participate in the affordability and arrearage forgiveness programs for which 
they are eligible. As discussed in multiple proceedings on these topics, increasing the 
ability of customers to pay their utility bills avoids service terminations and aims to 
decrease uncollectible expenses, which are recovered by utilities from all ratepayers. 

To further the Program objectives described in Section I.C, the Authority will 
maintain a QPL. Utility customers that call EOE seeking assistance with utility bill or 
arrearage payments, including enrolling in a payment plan or utility bill program, may be 
referred to the QPL to select a Provider to assist with the resolution of their issue at no 
cost to the customer. Providers will then provide eligible services designed to assist PSC 
customers with matters related to utility bills, arrearage payments, and service 
terminations. A referral from EOE is not required, and Customers can also seek eligible 
services directly from Providers. Providers will submit monthly invoices directly to the 
relevant PSCs for reimbursement. 

Docket No. 23-11-04 

Page 5 

A. 
ELIGIBLE SERVICES 
Services eligible for reimbursement are limited to “legal services with the express 
purpose of attaining participation in public service company programs designed to assist 
customers with utility bill or arrearage payments, including negotiating a reasonable 
amortization agreement . . . .” General Statutes § 16-262c (b)(8). Such services include, 
but are not limited to, reviewing customer documents, negotiating on behalf of a customer 
as their authorized representative, reviewing, drafting, and sending correspondence or 
otherwise communicating with a PSC on behalf of a customer, conducting legal research, 
and providing advice to customers. 

In its Written Comments, CCA provided examples of customer situations that 
would benefit from being served by the Program. CCA Comments, Apr. 19, 2024, 
Comments, pp. 2-3. CCA further provided examples of services it currently renders to 
customers that fall within the Program’s purview, including assistance in understanding 
how much a customer needs to pay under a payment arrangement, submitting verification 
of income, learning about available programs, reviewing customer bills to ensure they are 
enrolled in available programs, joining clients in calling their utility’s customer service 
representative, and assisting with next steps after service is terminated. Id. These 
examples are the type of legal services that are eligible under the Program to provide 
additional resources for customers to navigate their options presented by their utility. 
B. 
CUSTOMER ELIGIBILITY 
The CLAS Program is intended to supplement the existing resources offered by 
PSCs and to help customers that have not otherwise been able to attain meaningful 
participation in an existing affordability program. 

The Joint PSC Comments noted that the existing affordability programs are only 
for residential customers, and that they have not received a significant number of 
complaints from commercial customers. Joint PSC Comments, Apr. 19, 2024, p. 11. 
CCA supports prioritizing residential hardship customers. CCA Comments, Apr. 19, 
2024, p. 3. However, as demonstrated by the hundreds of thousands of previously 
unreached customers identified as hardship after data sharing with the Department of 
Social Services, CCA highlights that there are customers without a hardship designation 
but who qualify and may benefit from the CLAS Program. Id., p. 2. OCC supports aligning 
the participation criteria for the CLAS Program with the Stakeholder Group Compensation 
program, but does not believe that residential customer participation in the CLAS Program 
should be limited to hardship customers or customers residing in an environmental justice 
community. OCC, Apr. 19, 2024, Comments, pp. 1-2. 

The Authority finds that overly limiting Program eligibility may inadvertently exclude 
customers in need from using the resources provided. Therefore, the CLAS Program will 
reimburse Providers for providing eligible services to residential and small business utility 
customers, up to the statutory maximum of one million dollars each year. For the 
purposes of this Program, the Authority defines a small business customer as “a 
commercial or industrial electric customer with less than a two-hundred-kilowatt peak load 
that is a ‘small business’ under section 4-168a of the General Statutes.” Conn. Gen. Stat. 
§ 16-9c(a)(6). General Statutes § 4-168a(a)(2) defines “small business” as “a business 

Docket No. 23-11-04 

Page 6 

entity, including its affiliates, that (A) is independently owned and operated and (B) 
employs fewer than two hundred fifty full-time employees or has gross annual sales of 
less than five million dollars . . . .” 4 Consequently, small businesses would need to satisfy 
both size and electric consumption requirements, as applicable, to be eligible to obtain 
assistance from individuals or organizations providing eligible services under the CLAS 
Program. 

Accordingly, Eversource, YGS, Aquarion, UI, CNG, SCG, and Connecticut Water 
Company residential and small business customers are eligible to receive services under 
the CLAS Program. 
C. 
REQUESTS FOR PROPOSAL FROM QUALIFIED PROVIDERS 
The Authority will conduct a Request for Proposals (RFP) process using an 
application template (Application)5 to obtain information from individuals and 
organizations seeking to provide services through the CLAS Program. By prequalifying 
Providers before they offer eligible services and request reimbursement, the Authority is 
able to: (1) screen organizations and individuals for their ability to provide services; and 
(2) budget appropriately for each organization or individual within the $1 million annual 
statutory cap. Overall, a QPL will provide clarity to customers seeking assistance while 
minimizing the program’s administrative burden. 

The Application requires prospective Providers to include information about their 
organization’s services, including, but not limited to hourly billing rate, overhead and 
administrative costs, experience with utility advocacy, and language proficiency. The 
Authority will then review Applications and select Providers based on their qualifications 
and capacity to assist customers. Selected Providers will be required to assist customers 
of all seven covered PSCs, as needed. The QPL will also be publicly available on the 
Authority’s website. 

The Authority will launch the first CLAS Program RFP process in Fall of 2024 to 
select qualified Providers following the Decision’s issuance, enabling providers on the 
QPL to begin providing services on January 1, 2025. The Authority anticipates 
conducting a second RFP process in 2026 to provide an opportunity to update the 
Qualified Provider List and associated provider budget allocations based on applications 
received. Thereafter, the Authority anticipates conducting an RFP process every three 
years to allow for changes to the QPL; however, the specific timing and frequency of the 
RFPs are subject to change. 

4 The Authority applied the same definition in the Stakeholder Compensation Program. Decision, Jan. 3, 
2024, Docket No. 23-09-34, PURA Implementation of the Stakeholder Group Compensation Provisions 
of Section 15 of Public Act 23-102, pp. 3-4. 
5 The Application Template is attached as Appendix A. The Application form will be available on the 
Authority’s website and may be updated and revised from time to time. 

Docket No. 23-11-04 

Page 7 

D. 
DISBURSEMENT OF FUNDS 
1. Provider Budget Allocation 
The Authority considered multiple approaches to determine budgets among 
Providers to adhere to the overall $1 million annual Program statutory cap. OCC suggests 
dividing the budget equally among all selected Providers. OCC Comments, p. 2. CCA 
recommends allocating the budget based on the geographic area served. CCA 
Comments, p. 4. However, to approve a proposed budget for each Provider, the Authority 
must first understand the number of Providers that are applying for the CLAS Program, 
as well as their qualifications and bandwidth for offering services to PSC customers. 
Therefore, as part of its review of applications submitted, the Authority will determine a 
not-to-exceed annual budget for each Provider, considering the number of service 
providers to be included on the QPL, the requested budget, and the stated capacity of 
each provider. 

Once a total maximum annual budget for each Provider is set by the Authority, 
each budget would be subsequently subdivided to reserve funds for the customers of 
each PSC. The subdivision will be made in proportion to the number of customers of 
each PSC; see Table 1 below. Importantly, these PSC allocations are not binding, but 
rather serve as a general guideline for Providers as they track incurred expenses 
throughout the year.

Notwithstanding, customer requests for a given Provider’s services may 
necessitate adjustments to Providers’ initial budget allocations. For illustrative purposes, 
if Provider B is allocated a total annual budget of $250,000, but incurs $250,000 of eligible 
Program expenses within the first six months of a calendar year, the Authority may elect 
to allocate Provider B with additional funds from other Providers’ allocations if such funds 
have not yet been used by those Providers. As such, quarterly adjustments may be made 
to the Provider budget allocations, as needed, to re-allocate the remaining funding within 
each Provider based on year-to-date data to adjust for customer needs. This flexibility 
mechanism is intended to allow the Program to adapt to customer needs and inform the 
Authority of trends in how customers are using the Program. 
a. Advance Funding 
Some Providers may require advance funding to begin providing eligible services. 
Further, advance funding may facilitate diverse participation from Providers. In the 
Application, prospective Providers will identify the amount they require in advance funding 
to provide eligible services to customers and identify the specific start-up costs they 
consider necessary to furnish such services. Further, organizational financial statements 
will be required to demonstrate a Provider’s need for advance funding. Any advance 
funding will serve as a retainer for Providers to ensure that the eligible services are 
available to customers under the Program. Providers must return all unused portions of 
any advance funding at the end of a Program year. 

Once the Authority selects the Providers, the total amount of required advance 
funding will be allocated across all the PSCs covered under the Program, based on the 
total number of customers of each company. As the Authority cannot predict how many 
of each PSC’s customers will use the CLAS Program, the advance funding costs for the 
Program will be allocated to all covered under the Program using the proportions 
assigned in Table 1 above. The advance funding costs would later be reconciled based 
on the proportion of customers served from each company in the program year. The 
Authority may consider providing advance funding that represents less than 50% of the 

Docket No. 23-11-04 
Page 9 
Provider’s annual funding allocation to minimize the need for complex reconciliations. 
Moreover, the Authority may only offer advanced funding in the first year a Provider 
participates in the CLAS Program. 
b.
Overhead and Administrative Costs
Overhead and administrative costs are necessary for Providers to provide eligible 
services under the CLAS Program. Such a practice is consistent with other grant 
programs for direct legal services. CCA Comments, p. 4. CCA opines that the accepted 
range of an overhead and administrative cost rate ranges from 10-25%. Id. Under the 
Program, the Authority allows the use of an overhead and administrative rate of up to 
15%. 
2.
PSC Cost Allocation
PSCs will only pay for the eligible services rendered by Providers to their 
customers under this Program. As described in Section II.D.3, the Authority will review 
data reporting submitted by Providers to verify that the PSCs are charged only for services 
provided to their own customers. Quarterly adjustments to the allocations to each PSC 
within each Provider’s approved annual budget may be necessary, as described in 
Section II.D.1. 
3.
Invoicing
Providers are required to submit monthly invoices directly to the relevant PSCs for 
reimbursement by utilizing the Template Invoice provided in Appendix B. The applicable 
PSC will reimburse the Provider for the eligible services provided to the companies’ 
customers, as well as make any advanced payments deemed necessary by the Authority 
in its review of Provider Applications. Payments must be rendered within 45 days of 
receipt of an invoice. 
In addition, on a quarterly basis, each Provider is required to submit a report as 
compliance in this docket that indicates: 
•
The total invoiced amount for that quarter, broken out by PSC;
•
Number of customers served, broken out by PSC and by town;
•
Number of customers served, broken out by affordability program participation
(e.g. Low-Income Discount Rate, Matching Payment Program, flexible payment
plan, etc.);
•
The total number of hours billed by PSC; and
•
The total amount expected to be invoiced in the following month.
Each Provider’s quarterly report will be reviewed to determine whether and how 
funds should be reallocated to each Provider, as discussed in Section II.D.1. The 
Authority will subsequently notify the Providers of any reallocations within 21 calendar 
days of receiving the quarterly reports. This review is intended to maintain flexibility of 
the CLAS Program to accommodate requests for eligible services from customers to each 
Provider.

E.
PROVIDER ANNUAL REPORTING REQUIREMENTS
Providers are required to submit an annual report to the Authority by February 1 of
the following year6 that includes a summary of the quarterly report information for the 
entire previous calendar year, and additional data regarding the customers they assisted 
in attaining participation in a PSC’s payment arrangement or arrearage program; see 
Appendix C; Appendix D. Specifically, the annual reports shall include anonymized client 
data, including the town of each customer helped, the associated utility, the household 
income range, and a narrative describing trends. The service Providers are directed to 
file annual reports as compliance in the instant proceeding. 
The Authority may conduct annual review proceeding(s) to assess whether 
modifications are required to ensure the CLAS Program is providing equitable, statewide 
service, is efficiently serving customers, and is implemented efficiently by Providers. 
F.
COST RECOVERY
The PSCs may use deferred accounting for the costs incurred under the Program
and may seek recovery of such deferred costs in their next rate case. Carrying charges 
may not accrue on deferred expenses without explicit prior Authority approval. 
6 For example, a Provider would need to file an annual report by February 1, 2026, for services rendered 
in calendar year 2025.

APPLICATION TO PROVIDE LEGAL SERVICES 
Instructions: 
The Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (Authority or PURA) will maintain a list of 
organizations and individuals eligible to provide services (Providers) under the Customer 
Legal Advocacy Services (CLAS) Program as established in Docket No. 23-11-04, PURA 
Implementation of the Legal Services Funding Provisions of Section 30 of Public Act 23-
102. 
Providers will assist public service company customers with matters related to 
utility bills, arrearage payments, and service terminations. Provider(s) will be eligible to 
be reimbursed for the following services performed on a customer’s behalf: 
•
Reviewing customer documents;
•
Negotiating on behalf of a customer as their authorized representative;
•
Reviewing, drafting, and sending correspondence or otherwise communicating
with a public service company on behalf of a customer;
•
Conducting legal research;
•
Providing advice to customers; and/or
•
Other reasonable services that allow utility customers to attain participation in
public service company programs.
To be considered eligible for reimbursement under the Program, prospective 
Providers must submit a completed Application by filing a motion1 containing the 
Applicant Information below in Docket No. 23-11-04 no later than September 15, 2024. 
Selected Providers will be eligible for reimbursement for services performed between 
January 1, 2025, and December 31, 2025, and must submit monthly invoices, as well as 
an annual report that summarizes the services provided to utility customers. 
Applications will be evaluated on the following criteria: (1) grasp of scope; (2) 
credentials for this type of engagement; (3) experience for this type of engagement; (4) 
applicant’s approach to meeting the Program objectives; and (5) cost effectiveness. 
1 For information on how to submit a filing, visit PURA’s Make an Electronic Filing webpage.

B. INVOICING AND DATA REPORTING
The Authority will determine the annual budgets for selected Providers, subject to 
the overall $1 million annual statutory cap for the CLAS Program. The Provider shall 
submit invoices to the relevant public service company for services provided to customers 
on a monthly basis, as applicable. In addition, on a quarterly basis, Providers are required
